svg.desc: Before, forwarded edit-stack submissions were enqueued immediately, so annotations could become user input during an active agent turn. After, Portal claims one pending item only when the session is idle or a terminal output frame releases the next queued item.
svg.text: PR #2100 - Gate edit-stack sends on turn completion
Forwarded annotations used to inject during active turns; now
server-side queue promotion waits for a real terminal frame.

g.text: create_and_send_forward_edit_stack
Forward POST created stack rows and looped through
outcome.inserted, calling enqueue_input immediately.
That bypassed the old dashboard drain timing.
try_send_next_pending_edit_stack_item
Forward POST persists items, then asks one shared
server-side gate whether exactly one item may send.
If busy, the item stays status=pending.
Input ack made the session look idle
pending_inputs could be deleted before the durable
assistant transcript showed the active turn state.
A second annotation could slip into the same turn.
SessionManager.active_turns
mark_turn_input_delivered records a live turn when
enqueue_input or pending replay reaches the proxy.
The edit-stack gate refuses sends while it is set.
No terminal-frame handoff
Queue release was tied to browser behavior, not to
the agent protocols' result or turn.completed frames.
edit_stack_output_releases_next
Claude result/error, Codex turn.completed/failed,
and Muse run.terminal.* clear active_turns and
promote the oldest pending stack item.

svg.text: Scope: ordering guarantee only; this does not alter annotation capture payloads or agent protocol frame parsing.
